name: E-commerce and D2C brands
sector: 7.M Digital economy, social and public sector

problems.words: COD parcels keep coming back and we pay shipping both ways
quick_ideas: Confirm every COD order with the buyer before booking it, so unconfirmed parcels stop leaving
Go through last month's returns once by city and product, so you can see where they cluster.

workzap_build.text: a WhatsApp confirmation flow that messages every COD buyer, holds unconfirmed orders and shows returns by city, courier and product every day.

problems.ask_first: Do returns come mostly from certain cities or certain products?
problems.free_stops: The confirmation flow, hold rules and return-tracking set-up go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count returned COD parcels once by product and area this week, so you spot where failed deliveries are costing most.
Give one person the job of reviewing all returned COD parcels each afternoon, so repeat issues get logged before new dispatches.

problems.words: Courier says delivered but the money hasn't come in
quick_ideas: Match one courier's latest settlement against your delivered orders, so unpaid parcels show up
Send the courier one list of all unpaid parcels instead of chasing one by one.

workzap_build.text: a reconciler that matches every courier settlement to delivered orders each cycle and lists unpaid and short-paid parcels by courier.

problems.ask_first: Which couriers do you use at the moment?
problems.free_stops: How the matching runs across all couriers and order sources is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one recent courier settlement against your delivered parcels list, so missing remittance patterns stand out before cash planning slips.
Keep one notebook page for unpaid delivered parcels and one owner for updates, so courier follow up stays organised.

problems.words: Website shows in stock but the shelf is empty
quick_ideas: Count your best-sellers by hand and correct the storefront the same day, so cancellations stop
Note the reason for every manual stock change, so mismatches can be traced.

workzap_build.text: live sync between the shelf count and the storefront, with low-stock alerts on best-sellers before they run out.

problems.ask_first: Is the mismatch mostly on a few popular items, or across most of your catalogue?
problems.free_stops: The sync design and alert levels per product are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare shelf counts against website stock for your fastest movers today, so you see which items create the most cancellations.
Give one person the job of writing every stock movement in one notebook, so stock changes stop getting lost between sales and packing.

problems.words: Best-sellers sell out right when the ads are running
quick_ideas: Check stock on the products you plan to advertise before each campaign goes live
Pause ads on an item as soon as it gets low, so spend isn't wasted.

workzap_build.text: a daily morning read of best-seller stock against running campaigns, with alerts when an advertised item runs low.

problems.ask_first: Does it come up on most campaigns, or only when an ad suddenly does much better than planned?
problems.free_stops: Which products to watch and how alerts tie to campaigns is covered in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which advertised products went unavailable during recent promotions, so you see where demand and stock planning are disconnecting.
Set one fixed daily time to review ad-driven items before dispatch starts, so low stock gets noticed while action is still possible.

problems.words: Wrong size or colour going into parcels
quick_ideas: Give packers a printed slip per order instead of working from chats
Have a second person check a few sealed parcels each shift, so errors are caught early.

workzap_build.text: a phone pick-and-pack check that flags a wrong item before sealing and records errors by packer and product.

problems.ask_first: Is the mix-up mostly in size, mostly in colour, or equally both?
problems.free_stops: The scan-and-check process and its reports are detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count wrong size and wrong colour complaints separately for one week, so the bigger packing mistake gets attention first.
Give one person the final parcel check at sealing time, so size and colour mismatches are caught before handover.

problems.words: We spend on Meta every day but don't know which ad sold
quick_ideas: Give each campaign its own tagged link, so orders can be traced back
Compare spend against delivered orders, not placed orders, because returns change the picture.

workzap_build.text: tags linked to actual delivered orders, shown daily on one screen beside ad spend per campaign.

problems.ask_first: Which channels are you spending on right now?
problems.free_stops: How tags are set up and joined to courier delivery data goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare yesterday's delivered orders with the campaign names your team used in messages, so unclear attribution points show up quickly.
Give one person the job of noting the stated campaign source beside each order, so sales tracking stops getting skipped during busy hours.

problems.words: Customers ask "where is my parcel" on WhatsApp all day
quick_ideas: Send the tracking link with every dispatch, so buyers don't need to ask
Give one person a fixed time slot for tracking queries instead of constant interruptions.

workzap_build.text: a WhatsApp reply that reads courier tracking and answers parcel questions on its own, all day.

problems.ask_first: Do most of those messages come after dispatch, or before the parcel has even left?
problems.free_stops: The tracking connection and reply flow are described in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count parcel status chats during one busy afternoon and note their common timing, so you see when dispatch updates are failing customers.
Set one shared time to review parcel status questions together, so packing work is interrupted less through the day.

problems.words: People buy once and never come back
quick_ideas: Find which products bring the most repeat buyers and feature them more
Tell past buyers who agreed to hear from you about new drops, not just discounts.

workzap_build.text: a repeat-buyer and win-back list (counted in reports, never exposed) with scheduled restock messages to customers who gave permission.

problems.ask_first: Do the buyers who return mostly come from one product, or is repeat buying weak across everything?
problems.free_stops: The segments, timing and message plan stay for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many recent orders came from past buyers versus new buyers for your top products, so retention weakness shows by product.
Give one person a weekly list of past buyer follow ups in one notebook, so repeat sales activity happens on schedule.

problems.words: I don't know my profit per order after shipping, returns and ads
quick_ideas: Work out once what is left from one order of your top products after shipping, fees, returns and ads
Recheck your courier rate card, since rate changes slip by unnoticed.

workzap_build.text: a per-order profit view updated daily from product cost, shipping, payment fees, returns and allocated ad spend.

problems.ask_first: Do you already know the profit on your top few products, or has none been worked out?
problems.free_stops: How each cost is pulled in and allocated is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Write down one recent order from each top product with shipping, return and ad costs beside it, so thinner items stand out.
Give one person one notebook page per top product for order costs, so profit checks become part of the weekly routine.

problems.words: Orders from website, Instagram and Daraz are in three places
quick_ideas: Copy every confirmed order into one packing list at fixed times, so nothing is missed
Keep one shared stock figure for items sold on more than one channel.

workzap_build.text: a single order inbox pulling website, Instagram and marketplace orders into one packing queue for staff.

problems.ask_first: Which channel brings most of your orders, the website, Instagram or Daraz?
problems.free_stops: Which channels connect and how is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count for one day how many confirmed orders sit unpicked in each sales channel at closing, so missed handovers show where delays start.
Make one person own the master packing list during each shift, so orders from every channel reach packing without duplication.

problems.words: Eid rush — we can't plan how much to make or buy
quick_ideas: Pull last Eid's sales by product into one sheet, so this year starts from facts
Book supplier and courier capacity early, remembering Ramadan moves earlier each year.

workzap_build.text: a seasonal buying view from last year's sales by SKU, plus a daily owner read on orders, dispatches, returns and cash due during the rush.

problems.ask_first: Is the problem guessing quantities for each product, or booking enough staff and courier space?
problems.free_stops: The planning model and daily read layout go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which Eid items sold out earliest last season and which lingered longest, so buying follows real festive demand patterns.
Give one person the job of updating a single Eid prep notebook daily, so making and buying decisions stay aligned.

never_say: Any promise that returns will fall or ROAS will rise, or any benchmark return or conversion rate.
Advice on sales tax, VAT, GST/HST, customs or import duty — say "talk to your accountant".
Legal views on refund or return policy wording or consumer law — say "talk to a lawyer".
Anything that helps fake reviews, inflate orders, use competitor branding or under-declare parcel values.
Blacklisting or profiling buyers by identity, or asking for customer numbers, addresses or store logins.

sample_reply.person: Bhai returns ka koi hal batao, COD parcels wapas aa rahe hain aur double shipping lag rahi hai.
sample_reply.pi:
Ji, is ka rasta nikal sakta hai, aur pehla qadam aasan hai.
Pehle, har COD order booking se pehle buyer se confirm karein, taake bina confirm parcel na niklein.
Doosra, pichle mahine ke returns ek dafa sheher aur product ke hisaab se dekhein, taake pata chale masla kahan zyada hai.
Lambay arse ke liye Workzap ye set kar sakta hai: har buyer ko khud confirmation message, bina confirm orders hold, aur roz returns ka hisaab sheher, courier aur product ke saath.

Kya main aap ke liye solution document aur quote banwa doon? Mana bhi kar sakte hain.
